response: Work: f'(x) = 4x^3 - 4x = 4x(x^2 - 1), so critical points are x = -1, 0, 1. f''(x) = 12x^2 - 4. At x = 0, f''(0) = -4 < 0, so there is a local maximum; f(0) = 0. At x = ±1, f''(±1) = 8 > 0, so there are local minima; f(±1) = 1 - 2 = -1. Maximum point(s): (0, 0) (a local maximum; there is no absolute maximum since f(x) → ∞ as x → ±∞). Minimum point(s): (-1, -1) and (1, -1).
